source_quality.notes: A vertical third-party watermark interleaves into the text layer, so every displayed equation was read from a review proxy rather than from the extracted text. Printed footer page N sits two render pages behind the printed number.

task_reconstruction.summary: Quantify ninety years of popular music: rank the influential artists, test whether genre is really about sound, and locate the revolutions and the people who drove them.

section_map.summary: Summary sets a confident consensus against a quantitative reading and names Frank Ocean.
Section 1 builds the directed influence network and reports its structure.
Section 2 reviews prior influence measures and rejects raw follower counts.
Section 3 states four assumptions, each with its own rationale.
Section 5.1 assembles the influence vector from centrality and entropy.
Section 5.2 clusters the sonic variables into four original genres.
Section 5.3 scores the partitions with directed modularity.
Section 5.5 defines revolutions by centroid movement and names revolutionaries.
Section 5.7 sets the revolutions against the journalism.
Section 6 tests sensitivity to small genres, to the decay, and to the cluster count.
Sections 8 and 9 list strengths, concede the backward matching, and propose influence genres.
Section 10 is the letter to the society.

contributions.summary: A time-scaled Katz centrality that tries to stop older artists winning by longevity alone.
An influence vector stacking direct, indirect, within-genre and cross-genre scores.
Four sonic genres built by clustering sound alone, named after songs rather than traditions.
A revolution detector that reads the biggest decade-to-decade jump of a popularity-weighted centroid.

dependency_graph.via: the sonic genre supplies the fifth component
similarity to the later centroid weights them

assumptions.summary: An artist's first decade is their most influential, because revolutionaries acted early.
Every sonic variable and every influence factor counts equally, since any other weighting would be arbitrary.
Indirect influence accumulates geometrically over time, though the prose also says exponentially.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Thirteen sonic variables are given; explicit is dropped as a content judgement and key as non-linear, leaving eleven, scaled to the unit interval.
Merging the follower genre drops 809 artists with no primary genre, leaving 5045.
The subnetwork keeps only the top five genres and only artists first active in the twenty-first century, because fringe genres blow up the within-genre scores.

models.summary: Katz centrality with the additive constant replaced by the network order, then time-scaled.
K-means on eleven sonic variables with similarity as the reciprocal of one plus the distance.
Directed modularity of a partition and sonic contagiousness as a reciprocal mean absolute difference.

verification.summary: A neural network predicts established genre from sound at 0.0 percent over all genres and 63.3 percent on the four largest.
The same network recovers the four sonic genres at 52.0 percent against a 25 percent chance rate.
The adjusted Rand index between the established and the sonic partitions is 0.161, highest at four clusters.

results_trace.summary: Frank Ocean ranks first overall for 2000 to 2020 by the norm of the influence vector.
Established genres score modularity 0.38, sonic genres 0.17, and the top four established genres 0.31.
Mainstream revolutions fall in the 1930s, 1960s, 1970s and 1990s; the biggest sonic-genre move is in the 1960s.
Revolutionaries for the three mainstreaming revolutions were never computed, for lack of time.

writing_logic.summary: The summary opens on a consensus everyone holds, then replaces it with a number.
A failed classifier is not buried; it is made the reason for the next model.
The historical comparison reports matches and misses separately, and marks the misses as speculation.

language_observations.summary: Everyone believes they know, then Our goal was to, then This failure inspired us to.
We refrain from doing that for the sake of objectivity.
But how can we validate that these mean anything, answered by over twice the accuracy.
In the interest of time, we do not, owning a skipped analysis.
This speaks to the nature of the inquiry, where some elements stay subjective.
We have, we have, but what about, opening the future work.

visualization_observations.summary: Figure 1 draws one artist's one-edge and two-edge influences, the ego network that motivates the centrality.
Figure 3 plots time-scaled centrality against the decay and shows the two regimes later named direct and indirect.
Figure 5 plots the adjusted Rand index against the number of clusters, peaking near 0.16 at three and four.
Figure 6 tracks the similarity of each genre centroid to the mainstream centroid across five-year windows.
Figure 7 plots the change in centroid position over time for the mainstream, for one genre, and for the sonic genres, and the peaks are the revolutions.
Figure 8 plots the change in similarity to the mainstream with the 0.2 threshold drawn across it.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: A judge can check the revolution claim directly against the peaks in the centroid-change plot.
The cluster count is the one tuning choice defended by an independent index rather than by the objective alone.

weaknesses.summary: The time scaling exponentiates the negated centrality, so a more central artist scores lower and the ranking inverts.
The three revolution thresholds were chosen by hand to yield a few clear peaks.
The historical alignment starts from a revolution already found and then hunts for an explanation, which the paper itself calls biased.
Table 7 ranks an artist scored 0.47 above one scored 0.48.

independent_extensions.summary: The move from a failed supervised classifier to an unsupervised partition of the same features would transfer to any labelled network whose labels may not match its measured attributes.

unresolved_questions: Why does equation (2) exponentiate the negated centrality, which inverts the ranking it claims to preserve?
Why does the prose require alpha to exceed the reciprocal of the largest eigenvalue when stability requires the opposite?
Why does Table 6 report a contagiousness for key after the prose excludes key from the study?
What does the reported 0.0 percent neural-network accuracy refer to?
Which work does reference [1] denote in the summary footnote, and which in the body?
